name: no_flip
hypothesis: Disabling the momentum-flip exit (identical entries and stops, no HA-flip close) improves expectancy: the offline study graded the flip a mild drag but could not confirm it out-of-sample, so the live same-sample A/B decides whether the flip is retired.
stopping_rule: Settle when the paired same-sample 95% delta CI half-width vs baseline reaches 0.10R (n>=20, clusters>=8). Retire the arm if the upper bound (IID) < +0.10R. Retire the momentum-flip exit from the live config only if the clustered lower bound > 0 net @0.05 ATR -- the forward book, not the offline study, decides.
provenance: Settle bar (target_ci_halfwidth_r) recalibrated 2026-07-12 from the 0.15R placeholder seed to 0.10R -- the reviewed value, now equal to mde_r so a 'settled' verdict can distinguish a real edge from a dud rather than settling on an interval wider than the effect it tests. Experiment originally registered 2026-06-23 under sha 8a395ac927be12bfc1449e445cac6eae5f64fd72. Back-registered 2026-07-10 from the build_arms docstring in src/swing_screener/pipeline/arms.py; sha is the PR #64 commit that introduced the roster line.
decision: RETIRED 2026-08-15 -- FUTILE on the live forward book. Paired same-sample delta vs baseline: +0.003R over 2,810 pairs (498 tickers), 95% CI [-0.016, +0.018]; the IID upper bound sits an order of magnitude below the +0.10R MDE, so the pre-registered retirement clause fires. Reversal-only the delta is EXACTLY 0.0000 over 1,880 pairs -- the momentum-flip exit never binds on a reversal trade -- so the entire (null) signal came from continuation, now parked. Consequence: the momentum-flip exit STAYS ON in the live config; the arm asked whether disabling it helps and the answer is no measurable difference.

name: be_1r
hypothesis: Pre-partial stops otherwise never move, so every trade rides FULL initial risk to the end; ratcheting the stop to breakeven once the prior bar's high-water clears entry +1R cuts give-backs (21.6% of reversal trades that touch +1R close at <=0) -- the classic cheap high-information exit experiment.
stopping_rule: Settle when the paired_arm_delta 95% CI half-width vs baseline reaches 0.10R (n>=20, clusters>=8). Retire the arm if the upper bound (IID) < +0.10R. Promotion consideration only if the clustered lower bound > 0 net @0.05 ATR -- the paired same-sample delta, not the MAE study, decides.
provenance: Settle bar (target_ci_halfwidth_r) recalibrated 2026-07-12 from the 0.15R placeholder seed to 0.10R -- the reviewed value, now equal to mde_r so a 'settled' verdict can distinguish a real edge from a dud rather than settling on an interval wider than the effect it tests. Experiment originally registered 2026-07-03 under sha e4a8b7006a963cce3f8bc34bbac9796949e68fdc. Back-registered 2026-07-10 from the roster comment in src/swing_screener/pipeline/arms.py; sha is the PR #93 (2026-07 experiment queue) commit that introduced the roster line.
decision: RETIRED 2026-08-15 -- FUTILE on the live forward book. Paired same-sample delta vs baseline: -0.015R over 2,845 pairs (499 tickers), 95% CI [-0.040, +0.002]; upper bound below the +0.10R MDE. On continuation alone the ratchet is positive and significant (+0.010R, clustered lb +0.003, n=1,044) but an order of magnitude under the MDE -- a real effect too small to matter, in a book that is now parked. Consequence: breakeven_after_r stays 0.0 live; give-backs are not worth the conversion of winners into scratches at this size.
